beats.title: Shen Kuo Describes the Compass
beats.description: A Chinese scholar wrote down how a magnetised needle points south, the idea behind the hand-held navigation compass.
beats.note: Earliest clear written description of a magnetised needle in navigation; Dream Pool Essays dated c. 1088.

beats.title: Eyeglasses Appear in Italy
beats.description: Wearable lenses to correct reading sight were mentioned in Pisa, an early gadget people carried and put on at will.
beats.note: Earliest firm reference is a Pisa sermon of 1306 recalling invention about 20 years earlier; 1286 used as the commonly cited date.

beats.title: Lippershey Seeks a Telescope Patent
beats.description: A Dutch spectacle maker applied for a patent on a tube with lenses that made faraway things look close.

beats.title: Oughtred Builds the Slide Rule
beats.description: An English clergyman devised a sliding pair of logarithmic scales that let engineers multiply and divide on the go.
beats.note: Oughtred's circular and linear rules date from about 1622.

beats.title: Davy Safety Lamp for Miners
beats.description: A flame enclosed in fine wire gauze let miners carry a light underground without igniting explosive gas.
beats.why_in: a portable lamp carried by miners

beats.title: Laennec Invents the Stethoscope
beats.description: A French doctor rolled up a sheet of paper to hear a patient's heart, leading to the tube doctors carry in their bags.

beats.title: Friction Matches Go on Sale
beats.description: An English chemist sold sticks that lit when scraped, giving people fire in a pocket for the first time.
beats.note: John Walker invented them in 1826 and first sold them in 1827.

beats.title: Waterman Perfects the Fountain Pen
beats.description: An insurance salesman patented a pen with a reliable ink feed that could be carried in a pocket without leaking.

beats.title: Eastman Launches the Kodak Camera
beats.description: A small box camera came pre-loaded with film, letting ordinary people take snapshots and send it back to be developed.

beats.title: The Swiss Army Knife Is Born
beats.description: A Swiss cutler began supplying soldiers with a folding multi-tool knife that would become the ultimate pocket gadget.
beats.note: Karl Elsener's Soldier's Knife first delivered to the Swiss Army in 1891.

beats.title: The Electric Flashlight Debuts
beats.description: A battery and bulb in a tube gave people a portable light they could carry in a coat or a bag after dark.

beats.title: Kodak Brownie Hits the Market
beats.description: A cheap cardboard box camera sold for a dollar and made photography a pastime for children and families.

beats.title: The Thermos Flask Is Patented
beats.description: A German glassblower's double-walled vacuum bottle kept drinks hot or cold on journeys and picnics.

beats.title: Vest Pocket Kodak Is Released
beats.description: A folding camera small enough for a waistcoat pocket became a favourite companion for travellers and soldiers.

beats.title: Leica I Brings 35mm to Market
beats.description: A compact German camera using cine film showed that serious pictures could be taken with a device that fit in a coat.
beats.note: Leica I went on sale in 1925 after the 1913-14 prototype.

beats.title: Knirps Pocket Umbrella Appears
beats.description: A German inventor with a walking stick created a collapsible umbrella that shrank to fit in a bag or pocket.
beats.note: Patent records vary (1928, 1930, 1934); 1928 is the commonly cited invention year.

beats.title: Zippo Lighter Is Introduced
beats.description: A Pennsylvania company launched a windproof metal lighter with a hinged lid that clicked open with a thumb.

beats.title: The Biro Ballpoint Pen Is Patented
beats.description: A Hungarian journalist patented a pen with a rolling ball tip that dried instantly and could ride in any pocket.

beats.title: Motorola Handie-Talkie Goes to War
beats.description: A hand-held two-way radio let infantry talk to each other without wires, an early step toward carry-anywhere communication.

beats.title: Curta Calculator Introduced
beats.description: A hand-cranked calculator the size of a pepper grinder could add, subtract, multiply and divide anywhere.
beats.note: Wikipedia gives 1948 for the Type I; some sources say production began 1949.

beats.title: Regency TR-1 Transistor Radio
beats.description: The first commercially made pocket-sized transistor radio took music out of the living room and into people's hands.

beats.title: Sony TR-63 Pocket Radio Goes Global
beats.description: A Japanese shirt-pocket transistor radio was exported widely and started the country's reputation for miniaturised electronics.

beats.title: Kodak Instamatic Drops In
beats.description: A camera with a snap-in film cartridge needed no threading or fiddling, putting easy photography in millions of pockets.

beats.title: Motorola Pageboy Pager Launches
beats.description: A tiny belt-worn receiver beeped to tell doctors and workers to call in, the first widely sold personal pager.

beats.title: HP-35 Pocket Scientific Calculator
beats.description: Hewlett-Packard's shirt-pocket calculator did logs and trigonometry, making slide rules obsolete within a few years.

beats.title: First Mobile Phone Call Is Made
beats.description: An engineer walked down a New York street and rang a rival on a hand-held cellular prototype.
beats.why_in: the first hand-held mobile phone call

beats.title: Sony Walkman Hits the Streets
beats.description: A belt-clip cassette player with lightweight headphones let people carry their own soundtrack around town.

beats.title: Motorola DynaTAC Goes on Sale
beats.description: The first commercial hand-held mobile phone cost thousands of dollars, weighed about a kilo and needed ten hours to charge.

beats.title: Psion Organiser Pocket Computer
beats.description: A British calculator-sized device stored notes and contacts, an early ancestor of the personal digital assistant.

beats.title: First Text Message Is Sent
beats.description: An engineer typed 'Merry Christmas' on a computer and sent it to a colleague's mobile phone, the first SMS.

beats.title: BlackBerry Brings Email to Pockets
beats.description: A Canadian company's two-way device with a tiny keyboard let business people read and answer email on the move.

beats.title: Apple Unveils the iPod
beats.description: A white music player with a scroll wheel held a thousand songs and began to reshape how people listened to music.

beats.title: Steve Jobs Unveils the iPhone
beats.description: A touchscreen phone that was also a music player and internet device was announced to a hushed convention audience.

beats.title: Apple Introduces the iPad
beats.description: A slab-like touchscreen tablet bridged phone and laptop, and quickly became the default way to read, watch and play on the sofa.

beats.title: AirPods Wireless Earbuds Debut
beats.description: Cordless earbuds that paired with a phone and lived in a small charging case spread rapidly on streets and trains.

beats.title: Foldable Smartphones Reach Buyers
beats.description: A phone with a bendable screen that opens into a small tablet finally went on sale after delays and early screen failures.
beats.note: Samsung Galaxy Fold, retail release 2019 (announced February).

beats.title: Apple AirTag Tracks Your Keys
beats.description: A coin-sized tag attached to keys or bags could be found on a map by nearby phones.
